detector.name: Governance
detector.vulnerability_knowledge: Governance systems are vulnerable when voting power can be manipulated through flash loans or instant token acquisition, when proposal state transitions lack proper boundary checks, when critical parameters can be changed mid-vote, when member management allows re-addition of removed addresses, when external calls are made before state updates enabling reentrancy, when threshold calculations use incorrect comparison operators, when activation mechanisms lack spam protection, when value forwarding is missing in payable executions, when initialization omits zero-address validation, and when minting or parameter setting functions lack upper bounds. These flaws allow attackers to pass malicious proposals, block legitimate governance actions, drain treasury funds, or permanently break the governance process.
checks: Check if voting power snapshots are taken at proposal creation rather than at vote time, enabling flash loan attacks
Check if proposal state transitions use strict inequality (<) instead of <= for defeat conditions, allowing tied votes to succeed
Check if vote reclamation functions only block the currently active proposal but allow reclaiming votes cast in the same transaction before activation
Check if member addition functions lack checks against previously removed addresses, enabling re-addition of voted-out members
Check if proposal activation lacks rate limiting or spam protection, allowing dummy proposals to block legitimate ones via grace periods
Check if payable execute functions validate msg.value but fail to forward it in the external call
Check if initialization functions omit zero-address validation for critical roles like vetoer or token
Check if minting functions for governance tokens lack supply caps or upper bounds

incorrect_example.explanation: Multiple governance flaws: defeat check uses < instead of <= allowing tied votes to pass, executeAction validates msg.value but forwards 0, addMember allows re-adding removed members, setQuorumThreshold lacks bounds validation.

correct_example.explanation: Fixed defeat condition with <=, forwards msg.value in external call, blocks re-addition of removed members, enforces upper bound on quorum threshold.
